claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has yield strengths of approximately 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
HfMoTaTiZr should be processed by powder-bed additive manufacturing into a TPMS or gyroid lattice with 20–30% overall porosity.
The fabricated lattice should receive a homogenization treatment at approximately 1200 °C for 2 hours under an inert atmosphere.
The proposed lattice has struts 100–200 µm thick and unit cells 1–2 mm in size.
A TPMS lattice with the specified dimensions will efficiently localize and transfer mechanical loads.
Controlled lattice porosity reduces the global density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The lattice maintains sufficiently high local stiffness and strength in its load-bearing struts to preserve bulk yield strength.
Homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 hours will refine and homogenize the strut microstructure and minimize residual anisotropy.
The lattice intervention will reduce bulk density by approximately 10%, to about 9.2 g/cm³ or less.
The lattice material will retain a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
The lattice material will retain a yield strength near 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
The predicted performance applies under tensile and compressive loading at room temperature and 1000 °C.
Manufacturing precision and heat-treatment uniformity may affect retention of mechanical performance.
Stress concentrations at lattice-strut junctions may reduce load-transfer efficiency and mechanical performance.
The hypothesis is rejected if density is not reduced by at least 10%, room-temperature yield strength is below 1440 MPa, or yield strength at 1000 °C is below 770 MPa.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies 20–30% overall porosity, whereas the predicted bulk-density reduction is only about 10%. For an otherwise unchanged material, overall porosity and geometric density reduction should be directly related; the discrepancy is not explained.

The hypothesis and predicted outcome describe retention near 1600 MPa and 855 MPa, but the rejection rule permits strengths as low as 90% of those values. Thus, passing the experiment would not necessarily establish the stated near-baseline strength outcome.
